chunk_findings.detail: The rule first says a plain review runs when the item’s reviewed paths “differ now,” then says “A merge of main … is not new work.” That is wrong for a merge that changes one of the item’s reviewed files. Example: the last round recorded `src/foo.py`; the branch is then merged with main, and the merge resolves a conflict in `src/foo.py`. The tree at that reviewed path differs now, so the change should be new work, but the doc classifies the merge as not new work and would skip a reviewer. The exception must be limited to merges that do not touch any reviewed path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/review.py review.require_new_work doc

chunk_findings.detail: `test_full_and_the_knob_still_run_a_round` first calls `api.review(..., full=True)`, which re-runs the critic gate and records new untriaged findings. The subsequent `_plain` is then already justified by the “untriaged finding” branch, so the assertion passes even if `[review].require_new_work = false` is ignored or removed. This test does not actually verify the knob it claims to cover and gives false confidence in the new `require_new_work` behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_justified.py:66-71

chunk_findings.detail: Default `require_new_work=True` contradicts the adjacent, still-documented `review.fix_round_free=True` behavior. Concrete failure: an item changes only `src/a.py`; round 1 raises a finding on line 10. The author rewrites line 10 and settles the finding. `fix_round_free` says the next `ddflow review` should run a free delta review of that rewrite. But `require_new_work` sees the reviewed path set is still `{src/a.py}` and there is no untriaged finding, so it skips the reviewer with “nothing new to review” and counts no round. The fix is never reviewed, and this is the default for existing users.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/review.py:review.require_new_work

chunk_findings.detail: The test is confounded: `_triaged` leaves no untriaged findings and no changed paths, but the immediately preceding `api.review(... full=True)` call on line 79 runs a reviewer and does not triage any new findings that call produces. As a result, the subsequent `_plain` on line 82 is justified by “an untriaged finding”, not necessarily by `[review].require_new_work = false`; a regression where that knob is ignored would still see `out.exit == 0` and `rounds_used == 3`, so the test does not actually exercise the knob it claims to cover.

chunk_findings.detail: `_nothing_new` is called at the top of `_drain_review` and immediately emits `rounds used {used + 1}/{cap ...}` for any round that passes `require_new_work`, before the round budget check later in `_drain_review` can still refuse the call. For an item already at `[review].max_rounds` with `require_new_work = false`, `review()` prints `rounds used 5/4, justified: not required ...` and then the budget refusal, falsely reporting a fifth round as used when no reviewer ran. The "rounds used" line should be reported only after the budget is known to allow the round.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_nothing_new

chunk_findings.detail: The positive tests assert `_rounds_used(...) == 2` and `out.exit == 0`, but never assert `_runs(repo)` increased by one, even though `_runs` is already defined and used by the negative tests. Given an `api.review` bug where an allowed plain review increments the round counter and returns exit 0 but does not actually invoke the `critic` gate, `test_a_change_inside_the_items_paths_allows_a_round`, `test_an_untriaged_finding_allows_a_re_review`, `test_full_still_runs_a_round`, and `test_the_knob_off_runs_a_plain_review_on_a_settled_tree` would all still pass because they only observe the counter. The reverse omission also lets `test_a_main_merge_outside_the_items_paths_is_not_new_work` pass if the no-review branch increments `_rounds_used` without running the critic, since that test checks only `_runs(repo)`. The suite therefore does not lock down the core behavior that a reviewer actually runs exactly when the review is justified.

chunk_findings.detail: With `[review].require_new_work = true`, `_justification` treats `a["force"]` as an "asked for explicitly" justification, so `ddflow review --force` on an unchanged tree with all findings triaged invokes a reviewer instead of returning "nothing new to review". That makes `--force` a bypass of the require_new_work gate, contrary to [D-review-force-with-reason] ("It is not a gate bypass"). The decision permits force with a reason to exceed `[review].max_rounds`; it should not skip the new-work check.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_report_line_names_rounds_used_and_the_cap` calls `_plain(repo)` on an allowed re-review path but only asserts that the text contains `"rounds used 2/4, justified"`. It does not assert `_out.exit == 0`, that `_runs(repo)` increased by one, or that `_rounds_used` is 2. The previous missing-`_runs` objection still holds for this positive test: an `api.review` implementation that increments the round counter, emits this string, and never actually invokes the `critic` gate would still pass.

A buggy `_nothing_new` path for outside-path changes could count a round (increment `_rounds_used`) while running no reviewer, and this test would still pass with `out.exit == NOTHING` and `_runs(repo) == before`, contrary to the documented "counts no round" behavior.

It never captures or asserts `api._rounds_used(_state(repo), "critic")` before and after the forced review. An `api.review` implementation that actually invokes the critic and increments `_runs`, but fails to increment the round counter, would make the forced extra round invisible to `[review].max_rounds`; that is exactly the “gate bypass” [D-review-force-with-reason] says force is not, and this test would still pass.
